channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] France: Hundreds arrested as student protests escalate
item.description: Student protests have grown in scale and intensity, with violent clashes in some places leading to hundreds of arrests and dozens of injuries.

item.title: [DW] Five EU states plan first deportation center in Africa for 2027
item.description: Greece, Germany, Austria, Denmark and the Netherlands are moving forward with plans to establish deportation centers for rejected asylum seekers outside the EU.

item.title: [DW] Bosnia elections: Polls overshadowed by exhaustion, exodus and geopolitics as ethnic politics eclipse real problems
item.description: Bosnia goes to the polls on October 4 to elect several parliaments and presidents. While voters worry about the economy and emigration, the campaign is focused on ethnicity, exposing the country's political paralysis.

item.title: [Financial Times] Suspected Flydubai attacker received flight training in New Zealand
item.description: Co-pilot has been interrogated by Israel’s Shin Bet under UAE-led investigation into alleged attempted hijacking

item.title: [Financial Times] AI models used in bank cyber attacks, warns South Korea’s president
item.description: Lee Jae Myung highlights public anxiety over what one official calls a ‘completely new kind of crisis’

item.title: [Financial Times] How AI could scupper the dollar
item.description: Things are fine until they’re not

item.title: [Politico Europe] How Spain’s snap election could blow up Brussels
item.description: Spain’s snap election is poised to upend not just domestic politics … but EU politics, too. On today’s show, Zoya Sheftalovich and Ian Wishart break down the potential impact of the Madrid tumult — from the EU long-term budget to the potential puncturing of Ursula von der Leyen’s fragile majority in Parliament. Next, Hungarian Prime […]

item.title: [Financial Times] Sleep has always been a class issue
item.description: There is still a class divide when it comes to work that tramples over your body clock

item.title: [Financial Times] Surge in borrowing costs hits corporate America
item.description: Sharp sell-off in US Treasury market starts to feed through to junk-rated companies

item.title: [Financial Times] The bond market turns on France
item.description: The country is being hit by a pre-election debt sell-off. Many fear it could shake the Eurozone

item.title: [Financial Times] Andy Burnham’s Manchester City problem
item.description: The prime minister’s economic vision looks dangerously like a game of two halves

item.title: [Politico Europe] Der erste Machtbeweis der AfD in Magdeburg
item.description: In Magdeburg konstituiert sich der Landtag von Sachsen-Anhalt unter historischen Vorzeichen: Die AfD beansprucht als stärkste Kraft das Amt des Landtagspräsidenten. Mit dem Kandidaten Tobias Rausch und den entscheidenden Stimmen des BSW könnte dieser Plan aufgehen. POLITICO-Expertin Pauline von Pezold analysiert, warum diese Wahl die CDU zu Zuschauern degradiert. Im 200-Sekunden-Interview erklärt BSW-Vizechef Christian Leye, […]

item.title: [Politico Europe] Spanish election threatens to blow up Brussels’ political balance
item.description: Socialists warn a Sánchez defeat will alienate them in the Council and strain the coalition behind Commission President Ursula von der Leyen.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Tories want to duck Burnham’s social care fight
item.description: Three shadow Cabinet ministers told POLITICO the Conservatives might opt not to offer a rival proposal on the hot-button issue.

item.title: [Politico Europe] France’s debt troubles stir memories of the euro crisis
item.description: How long before Paris and others start looking to the ECB to rescue them?

item.title: [Politico Europe] France’s Mélenchon doubles down on student protests despite violent clashes
item.description: The presidential candidate is calling on supporters to join demonstrations Tuesday despite being accused of fueling unrest.

item.title: [Financial Times] India’s bullet train tangle leaves Japan fuming
item.description: Flagship high-speed rail project has been beset by delays, cost overruns and tensions

item.title: [Financial Times] Hong Kong quizzes HSBC over Singapore AI hub decision
item.description: Monetary authority strives to bolster Chinese territory’s status as international financial capital

item.title: [DW] Latvians head to the polls with Russia on their minds
item.description: On October 3, Latvians will elect a new parliament with Russia looming large over the campaign. Security fears dominate the agenda, but so does a debate over the economic cost of cutting ties with Moscow.

item.title: [DW] Nationalists top Bosnia-Herzegovina's divisive election
item.description: Bosnia-Herzegovina's three-member presidency is set to be dominated by nationalists from the three major ethnic groups, including Zeljka ​Cvijanovic, backed by disqualified Serb secessionist leader Milorad Dodik.

item.title: [EU Observer] Latvian PM holds onto power as Russia-Ukraine war shapes election
item.description: Despite its ordinary conduct, Russia's war still shaped Latvia's election in a new normal for Europe that most of us had hardly imagined just five years ago.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Explainer] Gas glut or supply crunch? And what it means for EU methane rules
item.description: The EU wants to delay its methane rules over worries they might disrupt gas imports in an already stressed market. Some analysts say even small changes would add to current price pressures, but a giant gas glut is coming and might arrive sooner rather than later.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] ‘Putin understands only strength’: EU envoy in Kyiv urges stronger air defences and hybrid-war response
item.description: Katarína Mathernová, the EU's ambassador to Ukraine, says Putin is boiling Kyiv 'like a frog', but she is determined to stay. She sees parallels between Hitler's Mein Kampf and Putin's essay which stated that Ukraine has no right to national existence, sovereignty or identity.

item.title: [DW] UK remands 2 Iranians over alleged antisemitic terror plot
item.description: The pair were arrested on the eve of Yom Kippur and later charged with plotting to attack Jewish targets in Manchester.

item.title: [DW] Bosnia and Herzegovina is still shaped by war, separatism, EU ambitions
item.description: Bosnia and Herzegovina is governed by a system established after the Bosnian war — more than 30 years ago. Ethnic divisions, a complex administration and European integration all shape the country's political reality.

item.title: [EU Observer] Brazil’s cliff‑hanger election could rob EU of key ally in Latin America
item.description: Brussels is watching as one of the world’s largest democracies heads to the polls on Sunday (4 September), with climate resilience and the Trump administration’s influence in the Americas at stake.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] AI threatens to deepen gender gaps — unless women seize the tools, says computer expert
item.description: From biased hiring algorithms to disappearing administrative posts, Bieliková argues that women risk being hit hardest by AI unless they seize the tools early and push for fairer, more accountable systems.

item.title: [DW] Merz, Macron seek tougher EU measures against unfair trade
item.description: Emmanuel Macron and Friedrich Merz have written to Ursula von der Leyen, calling for tougher EU mechanisms against unfair trade practices by other states. They name no names but seem to have China or the US in mind.

item.title: [DW] Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
item.description: A worker at a plague research institute in Siberia has died, and nearly 200 of her contacts are under medical observation. Russian authorities deny a link to the bacterial infection. The US is monitoring the situation.

item.title: [DW] Bosnia election: New steps to prevent electoral fraud, but nationalist parties remain on top
item.description: New technology has stopped votes being cast on behalf of dead or absent voters, and turnout has fallen to a record low. But it was a case of deja vu in Bosnia's elections with the same parties winning.

item.title: [DW] Hundreds of French schools shut, teen loses hand in protests
item.description: The student protests that rocked France last week have prompted authorities to keep up to 500 schools closed on Monday. A teenage boy lost his hand, seemingly while trying to pick up a police tear gas grenade.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Diplomat is Romania’s fourth prime ministerial candidate in five months
item.description: President Nicușor Dan gives Luca Niculescu the job of trying to break the deadlock and form a government in Bucharest, amid calls for fresh elections.

item.title: [Financial Times] Reflection AI boosts US ambition to compete with Chinese ‘open’ models
item.description: Start-up claims new model Beam is on par with leading Chinese competitor as battle with Beijing intensifies

item.title: [Politico Europe] America’s bomber withdrawal points to wider UK-US friction
item.description: The Pentagon's decision to relocate B-1 bombers from the British air base comes after months of frustration in the Trump administration over Britain's defense spending.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Sam Altman à Decoded : “Le monde devrait accepter que certaines choses négatives se produisent” face aux bénéfices de l’IA
item.description: Le PDG d’OpenAI a cherché à distinguer sa position de celle de son concurrent Anthropic en matière de réglementation de l’intelligence artificielle.

item.title: [EU Observer] Why ‘Made in Europe’ could push Burnham’s UK back into the EU’s arms
item.description: For UK Burnham, the growing risk of UK industry becoming collateral damage in an EU-China trade war is turning abstract talk of “better cooperation” into a stark choice between limited market fixes or a full-scale return to the EU table.

item.title: [Politico Europe] From the rent crisis to Trump: 5 things that will shape Spain’s snap election
item.description: Shifting attitudes toward the far right, fallout from the Ceuta crisis and the U.S. president's geopolitical maneuvers could have a major impact on the Nov. 29 vote.

item.title: [EU Observer] Women MEPs targeted by AI ‘nudifier’ apps push EU leaders to enforce December ban
item.description: If a woman enters politics, she may have to confront the fact that she may be one in 14 being digitally stripped by 'nudifying' technology. Such is what an EU ban is trying to stop: but whether it will be implemented in time, according to the Parliament's greens party, is far from certain.

item.title: [EU Observer] Putin and Vučić dominate Bosnia elections, as EU fades out of view
item.description: Last elections in Bosnia and Herzegovina might prove that Russia's influence is more broadly spread than the EU's.

item.title: [EU Observer] Spain’s 54-day sprint to the polls: can Sánchez’s housing gamble stop the far-right from entering into government?
item.description: Spain's Pedro Sánchez has called snap elections for 29 November, after parliament rejected his housing decrees, giving him a hot-button political issue for his election platform. But polls favour the opposition centre-right People's Party, which may need the far-right Vox to govern. And the loss of Sánchez would be a big blow for the centre-left in Brussels.

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘They want to shut me up’: Norwegian activist fights 20‑year Greek prison threat over asylum aid
item.description: Norwegian activist Tommy Olsen says he is facing enormous personal and financial costs over Greek allegations that he belongs to a criminal organisation, in a trial that starts on Tuesday in Rhodes.

item.title: [EU Observer] Russia’s army making no progress on the ground, but Kyiv’s old bridges are vulnerable to drone strikes (Ukraine Battlefield update, day 1,684)
item.description: Drone attacks on Kyiv’s ageing bridges risk paralysing commutes, trade and emergency services for hundreds of thousands of people ahead of winter.

item.title: [EU Observer] Trump cheers Bolsonaro Jr’s advance on Lula in Brazil, but EU fears for Mercosur alliance
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro is the favourite to defeat president Lula in the second round of Brazil's presidential elections, which could mean disaster for EU-Latin America relations.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Will Germany come back to nuclear energy?
item.description: Germany shut down its last nuclear power plants in 2023 but as the pro-atom far-right Alternative for Germany gains broader support, the country might change course.

item.title: [EU Observer] Russia is losing its grip on Kaliningrad, despite using the exclave for anti-Nato scare stories
item.description: Nuclear sabre-rattling only underlines the fragility of Russia’s grip on its trophy territory.

item.title: [EU Observer] THIS WEEK: EU trade chief heads to China as Brussels unveils long-delayed pre-enlargement reforms
item.description: The European Commission is expected to present its long-delayed pre-enlargement policy reviews to prepare for the integration of Montenegro, Albania, Ukraine and Moldova.

item.title: [DW] Spain's parliament rejects housing bill as protests continue
item.description: Spain's minority government suffered defeat in parliament as it tried to push through a pair of emergency measures aimed at making housing more affordable. A pensioner's eviction and protests led to the bid.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine, South Korea clash over transfer of 2 North Korean prisoners
item.description: A diplomatic scandal has erupted over two North Korean prisoners of war, with South Korea demanding an apology from Ukraine. What's been the reaction in Kyiv?

item.title: [DW] Turkey: Stock market scandal hits half a million investors
item.description: Asset managers are alleged to have artificially inflated the value of their funds. Turkish authorities have made multiple arrests, and a leading AKP lawmaker has resigned.

item.title: [DW] EU ministers mull new ways to curb irregular migration
item.description: The proposals include setting up so-called return hubs outside the EU and strengthening the border agency Frontex. Greece has even proposed temporarily suspending asylum applications in emergency situations.
